newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore noon shares firm, Hongkong Land lead.
newsitem.headline: Singapore noon shares firm, Hongkong Land lead.

text.p: Singapore shares were firmer at noon on Wednesday with Hongkong Land and its warrants accounting for about a quarter of the market's trading volume.
Dealers said trading in Hongkong Land was choppy with several rounds of profit taking well absorbed.

"There is a lot of speculative trading day with remisiers, traders moving in and out of the counter. It also shows there is very little else happening in the market," said a broker with a Singapore firm.
The buying frenzy in Hongkong Land is based on speculation that Hong Kong tycoon Li Ka Shing might launch a takeover of the company.
Dealers said some interest was also returning to US dollar denominated shares following their recent price falls.
Chinese drug firm Tianjin Zhongxin gained five cents to US$1.55 and phone cord maker Huan Hsin rose three cents to US$0.75.
The Straits Times Industrial Index stood at 1,955.81, up 4.10 points, at noon. Total volume was 135 million units with 196 gainers against 84 losers.
Leading gainer was Creative Technology, which rose S$1.60 to S$32.60 following overnight gains on Nasdaq.
Thai Prim fund led the losers dropping 60 cents to US$8.50, mirroring the weakness in Thai stocks.
